newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in Aug - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in Aug - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.8 percent in the four weeks of fiscal August versus July, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 6.7 percent when compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 6.3 percent in the week ended August 31 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
While sales for the month were revised down from preliminary estimates, August results were close to retailers' targets, said Jay Meltzer, managing director of Redbook Research.
"We began the month with slightly more upbeat plans than materialized, but now that the month is history it was certainly alright," Meltzer said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Many retailers undershot their initial targets for August, but only narrowly, Meltzer said.
Back-to-school items again drove sales last week, he said.
"Back-to-school is clearly better this year than last year," Meltzer said.
Sales projections for the coming weeks look "moderately bright," he added.
"The good news is that (stores') inventories are under control," Meltzer said. "That's a much better picture than it was at this time last year."
